Sampled ranking can reverse model comparisons relative to full-catalog ranking; increasing repetitions does not remove this bias ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). A 2025 study evaluates sampling through resolution, fidelity, exposure-bias robustness, and predictive power, using bootstrap intervals ([RecSys 2025](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086)). For this task, preserve pinned validation HR@10 as the selection criterion. Supplement with training-prefix target ranks, pairwise win rates, and popularity-stratified negatives. Popularity-matched hard negatives are a proposed stress test, not an unbiased substitute for full-catalog evaluation; unobserved items may be relevant.

Representation collapse should be measured spectrally: 2024 recommendation research documents low-dimensional embedding collapse ([Guo et al.](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/guo24e.html)). Entropy effective rank is exp(−Σpᵢlog pᵢ), with pᵢ=σᵢ/Σσⱼ ([Roy–Vetterli](https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/147929764.pdf)). Proposed diagnostics: measure item embeddings and centered GRU states separately, exclude padding, report spectra and variance alongside effective rank, and explicitly flag zero matrices. Low effective rank alone does not establish a harmful fault.

Controlled GRU4Rec fault injection remains a proposed validation procedure, not an established result from these sources: deliberately use count−1 readout on left padding, shuffle histories, zero recurrent states, or truncate representation rank. Require probes to detect their intended faults; positive score rescaling should leave ranking probes unchanged. Compare measured probe changes with actual validation HR@10 changes, using paired user bootstrap resampling within each category and recomputing the four-category macro-average. These intervals quantify user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fixed candidates and models; training-prefix diagnostics remain supporting evidence.
